newsitem.title: VATICAN: Castro invites Pope to Cuba in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Castro invites Pope to Cuba in 1997.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro invited Pope John Paul on Tuesday to visit his communist island next year, the Vatican said.

Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls told reporters after the Pope held an historic Vatican audience with Castro that no precise date had been set for the visit but that both men hoped it would take place in 1997 as they had discussed.

"Holy Father, I hope to see you in Cuba soon," he quoted Castro as telling the Polish-born Pontiff at the end of their 35-minute meeting. The Pope responded: "Thank you, my blessings on the Cuban people."

Cuba, one of the world's last communist states, is the only Spanish-speaking country in Latin America which the Pope has not visited. He is due to travel to Brazil next October, when a Cuba visit could be added.
Navarro-Valls said most of Castro's audience dealt with discussion about the role of the Roman Catholic Church in Cuba.
